name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
why: Stretches the front of the hip, which tightens with sitting, can tug on the lower back and shortens your running stride.
setup: Kneel on one knee on a cushion, other foot flat in front, like a proposal.
feel: A stretch at the front of the hip of the kneeling leg.
stopIf: Knee pain on the kneeling leg (add padding), or back pain.

media.credit: Video: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch (BSR Physical Therapy)

name: Couch stretch
why: A deeper hip-flexor stretch that also stretches the quads. Popular with runners and in long-hold flexibility routines.
setup: Kneel facing away from a wall or sofa, with one shin up against it and that knee in the corner on a cushion.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge.
cues: Squeeze the buttock of the back leg
feel: A strong stretch along the front of the thigh and hip.
stopIf: Knee pain, or pain in the lower back.
cautions: Skip it if deep knee bending flares knee-tendon pain.

media.credit: Video: How to Couch Stretch Correctly | Hip Flexor Stretch for High Performers Looking to Return to Sport (Ruben Parada)

name: Figure-4 glute stretch (lying)
why: Stretches the deep hip and buttock muscles that get tight from running and sitting.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the other knee.
cues: Pull the bottom thigh towards you
mistakes: Lifting the head and straining the neck
feel: A stretch deep in the buttock of the crossed leg.
stopIf: Pain at the front of the hip or in the knee.

name: Figure-4 glute stretch (standing)
why: The same buttock stretch without lying down, handy after a run or on the trail.
setup: Stand near a wall, tree or post for balance.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
cues: Sit back as if into a chair
mistakes: Letting the standing knee cave in
feel: A stretch in the buttock of the crossed leg.
stopIf: Knee pain on the standing leg.

media.credit: Video: Standing Figure Four Stretch for IT Band Syndrome - Vidpt (Vidpt)

name: Pigeon stretch
why: A long-hold stretch for the deep hip rotators and glutes, a staple of flexibility routines.
setup: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind that wrist, shin angled across your body.
Slide the other leg straight back and lower your hips.
cues: Walk your hands forward to go deeper
mistakes: Letting the hips roll to one side
feel: A deep stretch in the buttock and outer hip of the front leg.
stopIf: Pain in the front knee or at the front of the hip.
cautions: Can strain the front knee: use the figure-4 stretch instead if it hurts.

name: 90/90 hip switches
why: Moves both hips through rotation in and out, building the hip mobility that runners and desk workers lose.
setup: Sit on the floor with both knees bent to about 90 degrees, both knees dropped to one side.
Hands on the floor behind you for support.
cues: Let them fall to the other side
mistakes: Forcing the knees to the floor
feel: Movement and a mild stretch around both hips.
stopIf: Pinching at the front of the hip, or knee pain.

name: Clamshell
why: Strengthens the side glute (gluteus medius), which keeps your knee from caving in and your pelvis level when you run. Add a loop band above the knees when it gets easy.
setup: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent, heels in line with your bottom.
feel: Burn at the side and back of the hip.
stopIf: Sharp pain at the side of the hip.

name: Side-lying leg raise
why: Builds the side-hip strength that steadies the knee and pelvis on one leg. A key exercise for runner's knee and IT band pain.
setup: Lie on your side with the bottom knee bent and the top leg straight, in line with your body.
cues: Lift the top leg slightly behind you
feel: Work at the side of the hip.
stopIf: Sharp pain at the side of the hip.

media.credit: Video: Side lying hip abduction exercise to strengthen Gluteus Medius (Active Podiatry)

name: Banded side steps
why: Works the side glutes while standing, the way they work when you run and hike. Count steps in each direction.
setup: Place a loop band around your legs just above the knees (or around the ankles for harder).
Stand with feet hip-width apart in a quarter squat.
cues: Step sideways, keep the band tight
Knees push out over your toes
feel: Burn at the side of the hips.

name: Single-leg bridge
why: Loads one glute at a time, closer to what running asks of each leg, and shows up any side-to-side difference.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, then straighten one leg in line with the other thigh.
feel: Glute and back of the thigh of the working leg.
stopIf: Back pain, or a hamstring cramp that doesn't ease.

media.credit: Video: Single Leg Glute Bridge (Orillia Sports Medicine And Rehabilitation)

name: Side lunge stretch
why: Stretches the inner thigh muscles, which work hard on uneven ground and in side-to-side movements.
setup: Stand with your feet wide apart, toes pointing forward.
cues: Bend one knee and shift your hips over it
mistakes: Letting the bent knee cave in
feel: A stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.

media.credit: Video: How to do a side lunge adductor stretch (Rehab My Patient)

name: Single-leg deadlift

defaultDose.load: Bodyweight; hold a weight when it's easy

why: Builds hamstring and glute strength plus balance on one leg: just what running and downhill hiking ask for.
setup: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, near a wall for balance if needed.
cues: Hinge at the hips, back flat
Squeeze your glute to stand up
feel: A stretch and work in the back of the thigh and the buttock.
stopIf: Back pain, or sharp hamstring pain.

media.credit: Video: How to do a single leg Romanian Dead Lift: POGO Physio (POGO Physio)

name: Standing hip flexor stretch
why: The front-of-hip stretch without kneeling: handy at a desk or on the trail, where long sitting or a heavy pack tightens the hips.
setup: Stand in a long stride, back heel lifted, hands on your hips or a support.
feel: A stretch at the front of the back leg's hip.
stopIf: Back pain or a pinch at the front of the hip.
